name: 3D Explosion Selection
summary: For tightly packed 3D objects such as cells in a plant embryo: the user pushes all cells apart in an exploded view, controlling the spacing, so inner cells become visible and can be clicked directly.
howItWorks: The user controls the explosion distance, which moves every cell outward from the embryo centre while keeping neighbourhoods recognisable; the user then clicks the target cell and its neighbours in the 3D view. In a remote study with botanists' cell-division data (a 3D view operated with the mouse on a desktop), List and Explosion performed similarly for surface cells, List was better for traversing inner cells, and most participants preferred the Combination.
advantages: Reveals and lets users directly click otherwise enclosed objects.

relationships.note: The combination was preferred by most participants.
Also pushes objects apart to disocclude targets.

review.notes: Coded from the GI 2021 full text. The third technique, List selection, picks cells from a text list and is not a 3D selection technique, so it is not a separate entry.
